title: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala
facts_summary: The petitioner, head of a Hindu mutt in Kerala, challenged the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act 1969 and the Constitution (29th Amendment) Act 1972. The core question was whether Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 was unlimited, or whether certain basic features of the Constitution could not be amended.
holding_summary: By a 7-6 majority, the Supreme Court held that Parliament has wide power to amend the Constitution, but this power does not extend to destroying or abrogating the 'basic structure' of the Constitution. The basic structure doctrine was thus established.
outcome: The 24th Amendment was upheld. The 25th Amendment was partially upheld. The 29th Amendment was upheld. The basic structure doctrine was established as a limitation on Parliament's amending power.
